biggest_catch: Daily Transcription publishes no fixed pay rate — the official careers page says the pay rate for each assignment is only 'listed upfront' after you are inside and assigned work, so you cannot know what you will earn before qualifying; and pay is by mailed check (weekly) for US/Canada workers.
catches: Zero guaranteed tasks: you request time on their scheduler and are assigned work — the official page never promises any amount of work.

No fixed published rate: you only see the 'pay rate' per assignment once files are listed in the assignment directory (official page: 'pay rate... listed upfront so you can decide whether it's a good fit').

You must complete the career form, upload a resume, and pass their transcription test to strict standards ('Our HR team will only accept your test if you meet our strictest standards or are a course graduate').
Variable task availability: work depends on what you are assigned during your requested schedule — never guaranteed.

Effective hourly pay can be low: with no official rate published, earnings depend entirely on per-assignment rates and your speed; third-party reports (~$0.75-0.85/audio min) are NOT official and were not used.
Paid weekly by check only (US/Canada) — no PayPal/direct deposit option stated officially.
All transcribers are 1099 independent contractors — no taxes withheld; you complete a W-9/W-8 and handle your own withholdings.

eligibility: Official: must be 18 or older; must reside in the United States, Canada, or native-speaking English countries (for Transcriptionist roles; Subtitling/Captioner and Translation consider candidates outside US/Canada if bilingual). Some roles (Legal, Medical, As-Broadcast) require previous experience or course graduate status.

steps: Go to the official careers page https://dailytranscription.com/careers and choose the role matching your background (English/General, Legal, Medical, As-Broadcast, Spanish bilingual, etc.).
Click the link under the role to open its career form; complete the form and upload your resume (official: 'Complete the career form and upload your resume').

Watch for the automated test-instructions email from no-reply@wufoo.com (check spam) and complete the transcription test to their strict standards — 'Our HR team will only accept your test if you meet our strictest standards or are a course graduate.'
If accepted, request the time slots you want on their scheduler; you will be emailed when audio/video files are ready in the assignment directory.
For each assignment, review the media content, style, subject, pay rate, and due date listed upfront, and only take files that are a good fit for you.
Transcribe assigned files using your own computer, Express Scribe (or similar), and headphones; a foot pedal is recommended.
Get paid weekly by check (US/Canada); complete the W-9 (or W-8 outside the US) at onboarding — you are a 1099 contractor responsible for your own taxes.
timing: D.T. pays weekly by check only unless you are outside the U.S. or Canada, then other payment arrangements can be made.
